correctness.rationale: C PASS. The finite 2(N+1)-state CTMC is irreducible. Spin-reversal symmetry fixes mean N/2. For m=i−N/2 and conditional state s, the count generator gives L_s(m²)=b_s−c_s m² with b_s=N(a_s+h/2), c_s=4a_s+2h/N. Stationarity of m² 1_{environment=s} closes a 2×2 system with determinant c0c1+λ(r0+r1)bar c>0. Solving and subtracting fast-switch mean gives the positive numerator 8h(N−1)π0π1(a1−a0)². Differentiating its one-pole denominator yields strict negative first and positive second derivatives when a0≠a1. Equal-noise case constant; λ=0 used only as limit, never as unique-stationarity claim. Independent exact-rational finite CTMC stationary solutions for N=2,3,4 match the formula; proof is algebraic for every N.

Other PDMP/LNA and ordinary noisy-voter publications concern approximations or different settings. Method (second-moment closure) is classical, and equivalent telegraph-modulated exact moment results remain a realistic priority risk.

final_claim: For N≥2 two-opinion noisy voters with positive flip rates a_0,a_1, herding h and a two-state autonomous Markov environment with jump rates λr_0,λr_1, stationary count variance equals bar b/bar c + [8h(N−1)π_0π_1(a_1−a_0)²]/[bar c(c_0c_1+λ(r_0+r_1)bar c)]; for distinct flip rates it strictly decreases and is convex in switching speed.
limitations: Applies to autonomous two-state environment and complete-graph count dynamics; no mode classification, nonlinear network theorem or generalized environmental law.
